# Standings: MiniMax-M3.1 on node 0008 (generated by progress_page.py from runs_v3.json + runs_meta.json; do not edit)

SLA: A minute is in SLA when the median first token (TTFT p50) is under 3 s, median generation speed (TPS) is above 60 tokens/s and every request succeeds (success rate 100%). A load passes only when all 15 measured minutes are in SLA. The SLA changed on Oct 1 (before: TTFT p50 ≤ 1 s, TTFT p99 ≤ 15 s, errors ≤ 0.1%); every run with per-minute records is re-scored, and run notes written earlier still quote the old rule.

## Production readings

- Same requests as our replay, scored per minute with the same rule: 13/15 at 1.79 M; 12/15 at 2.24 M; 12/15 at 3.37 M; 8/15 at 4.44 M (test v3). In every scored minute of every valid run, production met the first-token and generation-speed rules (closest call: generation 60.1 tok/s at 3.37 M, minute 14); the minutes it loses are its own errors (504 timeouts on test v3.1; HTTP 429 load-shedding and 504 timeouts on the older test v3).
- Its own engine counters (Sep 30 13:29–13:34 PDT): 50.1 / 53.1 M TPM per node = 6.27 / 6.64 M per GPU; 436 / 476 req/min; engine TTFT p50 0.22 / 0.25 s; 128 running on b300-22 (32 per worker)
- Goal 7.00 M: basis not confirmed by the owner. Sep 30 notes tie it to production parity on production's engine counters ('north star ≈ production parity', timeline Sep 30 13:40; progress_data.json summary). Counted like production's engines it is 4.59–4.86 M on the request-log axis of our loads.

Retired methods (static frame, closed loop, v1 staircase) are no longer ranked (Oct 1); history in PROGRESS.md.
